decisions.reason: Although Product A never appears to have become a flagship offer, it fits the firm's core second-channel security capability and in a growing market its likely complementary value is enough to stay above a medium-sized firm's aspiration threshold for retention.

Product C gained its own page quickly and is tightly aligned with the firm's established authentication and end-to-end security strengths, indicating performance and strategic relevance above aspiration levels.

Product E also received a dedicated presentation and extends the firm's trusted-signature and hardware-based authentication portfolio, so boundedly rational management would retain it while results remain at least satisfactory and synergistic.

Product F seems to have remained a peripheral mention rather than becoming a prominent offer, so if its results stayed below aspiration levels management would reallocate resources toward stronger core products and new development projects.
